intent: A horizontal rule between sections of a Combobox's list.
typical_uses: A divider between two groups of items

dont_use_when.situation: A rule between sections of a page or a card, outside any combobox

invariants.text: combobox.module.css pulls the rule out by the list's padding on both sides, so it runs edge to edge across the popup, and gives it vertical margin of its own.
combobox.module.css draws only a horizontal rule; `orientation` changes the announced `aria-orientation`, not the drawing.
The separator renders with role `separator`, takes no pointer events and is not an option that arrow keys land on.

anti_patterns.dont: Put a separator first or last in the popup, or two in a row
anti_patterns.do_instead: Place separators only between items or groups; a rule at an edge or doubled draws a break with nothing on one side

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: The kit's standalone Separator inside the list
bad.why: The list accepts ComboboxSeparator, whose margins are set against the list's padding; a general Separator stops short of the popup's edges.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SeparatorState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.
